title: ElevenLabs Realtime: Scribe v2 Pricing and Features
summary: ElevenLabs Realtime transcribes speech while people are still talking, not after recordings end.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces has already shipped for ElevenLabs


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/elevenlabs) has an ElevenLabs integration, and like every connected integration it is available to an AI as a tool. Talk time is the cost driver, and what you pay for stays unchanged whichever way the audio reaches the workflow.


### The dated release and link


Activepieces has an ElevenLabs integration, and like every connected integration it is available to an AI as a tool.


Being available as a tool means an agent can use the integration directly, without a separate build.


That integration is not a separate agent catalog you have to rebuild.


Once the ElevenLabs integration is connected in Activepieces, an agent can call it: the same action that runs as a step in a flow is also exposed as a tool on the MCP server each project gets, which Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent of your own can use.


Nothing is exported or wired a second time, and you can read the mechanism in packages/integrations in the MIT-licensed repo.


Check that your key's scopes match the actions you enable.


The integration itself lists 2 actions and 0 triggers. Nothing in it fires when a person starts speaking, and it has no step named for Realtime.


### Connecting it in a workflow today


You can reach Realtime through an HTTP step. Because the integration has no trigger, something else must start the flow, such as a webhook or a schedule. The HTTP step then calls ElevenLabs directly, authenticated with the same API key.


We didn't run or test Realtime through this path. This describes what the pages show, not a verified build.


The consequence is that you own the connection handling the integration would otherwise hide.
